concept.name: Initial margin
concept.definition: The minimum collateral or equity required when a new leveraged position is opened, under the applicable regulatory, exchange, clearing, and house rules.
concept.intuition: It links the capital posted by a trader to the larger exposure and credit risk carried in the account.
concept.mechanics: Before accepting the position, calculate required initial margin from purchase value or risk model and compare it with eligible account collateral.
concept.formula: Initial margin ratio = required initial equity / position market value
concept.failure_modes: House requirements can rise without notice, prices can gap, and forced liquidation or interest can make losses exceed the initial capital posted.
concept.misconceptions: Margin is collateral or account equity, not a fixed maximum loss; leverage magnifies gains and losses on the trader's equity.
concept.example: At a 50% initial requirement, buying $10,000 of eligible stock requires $5,000 of initial equity.
